outlets.name: Globe
outlets.notes: Menu (Dec 2025) hosted on heathrow.com says 'All our chicken is halal.' The same menu includes bacon dishes.
outlets.claim: The restaurant’s menu on Heathrow’s website says “All our chicken is halal.” The same menu includes bacon dishes, so ask about your order.

airport_note: No outlet with a halal claim was found on the official airport site or a certifier list on 13 Oct 2026. Ask at the airport information desk or the outlet. heathrow.com was searched site-wide for "halal" and returned no restaurant claim; pages read (e.g. wagamama, Harris + Hoole) do not mention halal. Third-party guides naming Heathrow outlets (HalalTrip) are undated and unverified.

outlets.name: Nando's
outlets.certifier: Not named. Nando's says its halal chicken is 'authorised by leading Halal Food Authorities' and is pre-stunned.
outlets.notes: Listed on Nando's halal page as 'Gatwick - South Terminal' (airside). Gatwick's breakfast page also says 'Halal chicken available' (https://www.gatwickairport.com/restaurant-directory/breakfast.html). Halal applies to chicken only; the restaurant serves other items. Pre-stunned chicken is not accepted by some Muslims (HMC standard).

airport_note: One outlet with a verified halal-chicken claim. Ask the outlet.

outlets.name: Wrapchic
outlets.notes: The page says 'Find us in Terminal 2 Arrivals'. Its text does not say halal; only the photo description mentions a 'Halal' sign on the storefront. Manchester's restaurants page has a Halal filter, but its results could not be read (JavaScript).
outlets.claim: A photo description on the airport’s website mentions a halal sign at this outlet. We haven’t verified the current menu.

airport_note: The official restaurants page offers a Halal dietary filter (https://www.manchesterairport.co.uk/at-the-airport/restaurants/); its outlet list could not be read on 13 Oct 2026. Ask the outlet.

airport_note: The Chaiiwala page (Wayback capture of 15 Aug 2025) does not mention halal. Ask the outlet.

Muslim-majority: halal is widely the default. Non-halal food is regulated, not banned: Dubai requires a permit to sell pork and enforces rules on handling it (Gulf News, 2013: https://gulfnews.com/uae/government/tough-penalties-for-flouting-rules-on-pork-sales-1.1141799). GCC halal food standard: GSO 2055-1. Ask the outlet.

Muslim-majority: halal is widely the default, but certification is voluntary and alcohol is sold. Ask the outlet.
